sections.html: Currently two species of the genus Tanichthys are known in the hobby: the White Cloud Mountain minnow Tanichthys albonubes and the Jewel Minnow, T. micagemmae. The White Cloud is available exclusively as bred specimens, whereas the Jewel minnow is also imported as wild-collected fish. The Jewel minnow was discovered in 2001 in Central Vietnam.
The maximum size of the Jewel minnow is less than 3 cm, so the species is an ideal fish for so-called nano aquariums.
If they are kept in a single-species tank, no additional heater is necessary in indoor aquariums.
The Jewel minnow should be kept and bred in schools. The fish are completely peaceful with any other fish.
Males and females can easily be distinguished by the shape and colour of the dorsal and anal fins, which are much larger and more colourful in males.

The species spawns in fine plant material. The offspring swim close under the water surface. If the parents are fed properly and with a good variety of food, usually some of the young survive even in a community tank (surface plants are necessary, especially Riccia).
Tanichthys micagemmae is a real gem and every fishkeeper should have tried it.
